lines.en: scene whatwelove1
Thank you for purchasing the November 2022 Lessons in Love Care Package and welcome to the scene commentary for Ayane Amamiya’s event “Prisoner!”
lines.zh: 感谢你购买 2022 年 11 月的《Lessons in Love》内容包，欢迎来到 Ayane Amamiya 事件「囚徒！」的场景解说。

lines.en: Prisoner is just one of the many larger “Wtf” moments in my game, but its timing (Which coincided with the first update I ever got to work on full-time) was one of the {i}first{/i} times I ever truly got to hurt someone.
lines.zh: 《囚徒》只是我游戏里众多「卧槽」时刻之一，但它出现的时间点（正好赶上我第一次全职做更新）是我{i}头几次{/i}真正伤害到某个人的时刻之一。

lines.en: And before you get any ideas, no. I’m not talking about you. I’m talking about Ayane- a character who is very close to my heart and, at oftentimes, feels a lot like a daughter to me.
lines.zh: 在你多想之前，先说清楚：不是，我说的不是你。我说的是 Ayane——一个我很珍视的角色，而且很多时候，她对我来说很像女儿。

lines.en: Now, you’re probably wondering- {i}Selebus! Why involve your daughter in a situation that leads to immense psychological trauma! And why do you take her clothes off so much?!{/i}
lines.zh: 你大概会想问——{i}Selebus！为什么要把你的女儿放进一个会造成巨大心理创伤的处境里！还有你为什么老是把她的衣服脱掉？！{/i}

lines.en: And to that I’d say “Fuck you” because I don’t have to explain anything and you just have to listen to me because that is how this shit works.
lines.zh: 对此我只想说「去你的」——因为我不需要解释任何东西，你只要听我说就行，因为这玩意儿就是这么运作的。

lines.en: : Get on with it, Dad. We all know that everyone is just here for me.
lines.zh: : 别废话了，老爸。大家都知道，所有人来这儿就是为了我。

lines.en: : Sorry, Ayane. And sorry even more for making you relive this trauma for the sake of our subscribers.
lines.zh: : 抱歉，Ayane。更抱歉的是为了我们的订阅者，让你重新经历一次这个创伤。

lines.en: : If that’s what it takes to get the cash rolling in, so be it. Besides, I have a history of being neglected by fathers, so this is nothing to me.
lines.zh: : 如果非这样钱才能进来，那就这样吧。再说，我被父亲忽视也不是一次两次了，所以这对我来说不算什么。

lines.en: scene black

Prisoner, which was actually originally titled “What We Love,” is, all things considered, a scene about the downfall of incessant lust and how acting on impulses can sometimes lead to terrible consequences.
lines.zh: 《囚徒》原本其实叫「我们所爱的东西」。总的来说，它讲的是无休止的欲望如何走向崩坏，以及凭冲动行事有时会带来可怕的后果。

lines.en: scene whatwelove35
Up until Prisoner, lust scenes had been fun ways to both bang and grow closer to the characters of the game.
lines.zh: 在《囚徒》之前，欲望戏一直是既能爽、又能跟游戏角色拉近距离的有趣方式。

lines.en: And while some people would happily equate non-consensual sex in video games to “fun,” I’m moreover referring to how the character in question saw the event.
lines.zh: 虽然有些人很乐意把游戏里的非自愿性行为等同成「好玩」，但我更想说的是那个角色自己是怎么看待这件事的。

lines.en: While you, the player, were still able to reap the benefits of your (sometimes literal) grinding, the one who truly faced the consequences of untamed lust was Ayane.
lines.zh: 你作为玩家依然能收获（有时是字面意义上的）刷数值带来的好处，但真正承担未加约束的欲望之后果的，是 Ayane。

lines.en: Lessons in Love is a commentary on all sorts of things and, at many times, a critique on the market I decided to place myself in when I made this game.
lines.zh: 《Lessons in Love》是对各种东西的评论，很多时候也是在批判我做这款游戏时选择投身其中的那个市场。

lines.en: In a lot of western h-games (This one included), the player is encouraged and sometimes coaxed into mindlessly grinding stats in an effort to uncover what’s next.
lines.zh: 在很多欧美 H 游戏里（包括这一款），游戏会鼓励、有时甚至诱导玩家无脑刷数值，只为挖出下一段内容。

lines.en: But a great idea to me was showing players what would happen if this was taken too far.
lines.zh: 但对我来说，一个很棒的想法是：向玩家展示如果这事做过头了会怎样。

lines.en: What if constantly having sex with a character and, in turn, increasing their desire to do things like that became destructive?
lines.zh: 如果不断和某个角色做爱、进而让她越来越想做这种事，最后变成一种破坏性的东西呢？

lines.en: scene whatwelove36
What if doing so created a major rift or divide in the relationship between two characters?
lines.zh: 如果这样做在两个角色的关系里撕开一道巨大的裂痕呢？

lines.en: scene whatwelove37
Enter Kirin Kanda- a long time “friend” of Ayane, but one who would sooner prioritize her own interests over hers even if it meant damaging one of the few relationships she has.
lines.zh: 于是 Kirin Kanda 登场了——她是 Ayane 多年的「朋友」，但一个宁愿把自己的利益放在她前面的人，哪怕这意味着要毁掉她为数不多的一段关系。

lines.en: : I really hope I’m getting paid overtime for this. I had shit to do today.
lines.zh: : 我真希望这段能拿加班费。我今天本来还有一堆破事要干。

lines.en: scene whatwelove41 with flash
: You’re not the only one, you fucking whore.
lines.zh: : 又不只有你一个人，你这贱货。

lines.en: : Jesus, Ayane. It’s been like two years. Get over yourself.
lines.zh: : 天哪，Ayane。都过去两年了。别再纠结了。

lines.en: What ensued shortly after Kirin entered the room would forever affect Ayane’s life in a depressingly meaningful way and teach not just the player but {i}her{/i} about the consequences I mentioned before.
lines.zh: Kirin 进屋后紧接着发生的事，以一种令人压抑的深刻方式永远改变了 Ayane 的人生，也让玩家、更让她{i}自己{/i}明白了我前面说的那些后果。

lines.en: About how life is never truly carefree and how everything that’s good in it can be flipped on its head without so much as a warning if you become too complacent.
lines.zh: 明白了人生从来不是真正无忧无虑的，也明白了只要你太过得意，其中一切美好的东西都可能在毫无预警的情况下被彻底翻转。

lines.en: And if Sensei wasn’t so far gone at the time of this happening, he probably would have realized that too.
lines.zh: 如果 Sensei 在事情发生时还没陷得那么深，他大概也会意识到这一点。

lines.en: But it was {i}he{/i} who did this. And it’s {i}he{/i} who does {i}everything{/i} at your behest.
lines.zh: 但做下这件事的是{i}他{/i}。听你命令行事的，也都是{i}他{/i}。

lines.en: He’s benefiting in the same exact way you are.
lines.zh: 他得到的好处，跟你得到的一模一样。

lines.en: scene meintheroom1 with flash
: It’s hard to understand how much you love something until that love is threatened. Until you think you’re just a step or two away from losing it all- which is exactly how Ayane felt in that moment.
lines.zh: : 很难真正明白自己有多爱一样东西，除非那份爱受到了威胁。除非你觉得再走一两步就会失去一切——而那一刻的 Ayane 正是这么想的。

lines.en: : It was less about the fact that she was being literally sexually assaulted by a friend, but what this would mean for the future with the man she loves.
lines.zh: : 重点其实不在于她正被一个朋友实质性侵犯，而在于这对她和她所爱的那个男人的未来意味着什么。

lines.en: : Would he flag this as careless? Leave her behind just like her father did because of a compulsion {i}he{/i} had to just use her a fuck toy?
lines.zh: : 他会把这当成她不自重吗？会因为{i}他自己{/i}那种把她当泄欲工具的冲动，像她父亲那样把她抛下吗？

lines.en: : She didn’t know. And that’s what scared her.
lines.zh: : 她不知道。而这才让她害怕。

lines.en: : And when people are scared, they’ll usually do what they’re told.
lines.zh: : 而人一旦害怕，通常会照别人说的做。

lines.en: scene meintheroom2 with flash
: Which brings us to today- a point in time where she allows herself to be swallowed by these uncertainties and willingly subjects herself to repeated sexual torment because she is afraid.
lines.zh: : 于是就到了今天——她听任自己被这些不确定吞没，因为害怕而主动承受一次又一次的性折磨。

lines.en: : It is also at this point that I will answer some of your questions.
lines.zh: : 也正是在这里，我来回答你们的一些提问。

lines.en: : {b}Question 1: How early on in development was Prisoner planned?{/b}
lines.zh: : {b}问题一：《囚徒》在开发多早就规划好了？{/b}

lines.en: : From the very beginning, (And this is a bit less prevalent after the revamp of Chapter 1) Ayane was shown as a character who was, for lack of a better term, destructively horny.
lines.zh: : 从一开始（在第一章重做之后这点稍微不那么明显了），Ayane 就被塑造成一个——找不到更好的词——「毁灭性地发情」的角色。

lines.en: : I always knew there would be repercussions for this and that {i}someone{/i} was going to walk in at the wrong time, but I didn’t know {i}who{/i} until the update in which the event was released.
lines.zh: : 我一直知道这会招来报应，也知道{i}某个人{/i}会在最不该出现的时候走进来，但直到发布这个事件的那个更新，我才确定{i}是谁{/i}。

lines.en: : {b}Question 2: Given how much story impact Prisoner has for the story arcs of both Ayane and Kirin, why is it optional?{/b}
lines.zh: : {b}问题二：《囚徒》对 Ayane 和 Kirin 两条故事线影响这么大，为什么它是可选的？{/b}

lines.en: : The reasons I’ve mentioned earlier in this commentary about how overindulging in certain things can cause unforeseen consequences is essentially my answer to this question.
lines.zh: : 我在解说前面提到的那些——过度沉溺于某些东西会招致意料之外的后果——基本上就是我对这个问题的回答。

lines.en: : Despite the ripple effect Prisoner has on the relationship between these two girls, the fact that it can be missed entirely mimics how {i}real{/i} relationships work to me.
lines.zh: : 尽管《囚徒》对这两个女孩的关系有涟漪般的连锁影响，但它完全可能被错过这件事，在我看来正像是{i}现实{/i}中关系的运作方式。

lines.en: : There are plenty of people I’ve met in my life that I’ve fallen out of favor with after just one event or, in some cases, even one discussion.
lines.zh: : 我这辈子认识过不少人，只因为一件事、有时候甚至只因为一次谈话，就和他们疏远了。

lines.en: : Lessons in Love should be no different from that. And I don’t regret implementing the event in this way as I believe there is a universe out there where Ayane and Kirin {i}can{/i} remain friends.
lines.zh: : 《Lessons in Love》也不该例外。而且我并不后悔用这种方式做这个事件，因为我相信在某个宇宙里，Ayane 和 Kirin {i}是能{/i}继续做朋友的。

lines.en: : Just not the universe most players found themselves in.
lines.zh: : 只是大多数玩家所处的那个宇宙不行。

lines.en: : {b}Question 3: Was Kirin joining the main cast already established by the time you made Prisoner? Or was that brought into existence {i}because{/i} of Prisoner.
lines.zh: : {b}问题三：你做《囚徒》的时候，Kirin 加入主角团这件事已经定了吗？还是说那是因为《囚徒》才有的？

lines.en: : Prisoner’s existence has nothing to do with whether or not Kirin was going to join the main cast. That was something that I planned on doing from the moment I first started talking about a second floor.
lines.zh: : 《囚徒》的存在和 Kirin 会不会加入主角团没关系。那是我从开始讲「二楼」这件事起就打算做的。

lines.en: : Kirin was actually supposed to join the class {i}earlier,{/i} but I decided to save her for later as she was already a major character in the story and I didn’t believe she’d work well alongside Molly.
lines.zh: : Kirin 本来是要{i}更早{/i}加入班级的，但我决定把她留到后面，因为她在故事里已经是重要角色了，而且我觉得她和 Molly 放在一起效果不好。

lines.en: : {b}Question 4: Did the community reaction to Prisoner live up to what you hoped it would be? And what was it like essentially painting a target on a character’s back?{/b}
lines.zh: : {b}问题四：玩家对《囚徒》的反应达到你的预期了吗？还有，等于在角色背上画个靶子，那是什么感觉？{/b}

lines.en: : The community reacted {i}exactly{/i} how I wanted them to- and this wound up being a major confidence booster for me as I felt it was the first time I {i}truly{/i} got through the people in the game.
lines.zh: : 玩家的反应{i}完全{/i}就是我想要的样子——这成了我信心上的一剂强心针，因为我觉得那是第一次我{i}真正{/i}把话传达到了玩这款游戏的人心里。

lines.en: : Prior to the beach update, I was working over 80 hours a week between Lessons in Love and my job at a law firm and wasn’t able to give it the love it deserved. But for the beach, I was.
lines.zh: : 在海滩那次更新之前，我一边做《Lessons in Love》、一边在律所上班，一周要干 80 多个小时，没法给它应有的那份心力。但海滩那次，我给到了。

lines.en: : And it was because of this outpouring of strong emotions that I knew this game was going to be something special and that I was going to touch so many more people in so many more ways.
lines.zh: : 正是因为这样汹涌而强烈的情绪，我才确定这游戏会成为特别的东西，也确定我会以更多方式打动更多的人。

lines.en: : In regard to painting a target on a character’s back, I believe this is something all good writers must do at times.
lines.zh: : 至于在角色背上画靶子这件事，我觉得这是所有好作家偶尔都必须做的事。

lines.en: : Having a world full of nothing but “good guys” is boring.
lines.zh: : 一个世界里全是「好人」，那很无聊。

lines.en: : And when real life is filled with so many bad people, the idea of them just not existing because I’m afraid of someone being disliked just doesn’t make sense to me.
lines.zh: : 现实里有那么多坏人，却因为怕某个角色被讨厌就不让他们存在，这在我看来根本说不通。

lines.en: : The fact that this event caused so many people to hate Kirin shows just how good of a character she is because she exists to be hated. And you don’t use words like that on characters who aren’t worth it.
lines.zh: : 这个事件让那么多人恨 Kirin，恰恰说明她这个角色有多好——因为她存在的意义就是被恨。而你不值得的角色，是不会让你用这种词的。

lines.en: : I’m going to make you hate people because I want to move you. And one way of doing that is making you rethink the way you look at certain characters with malleable resolves.
lines.zh: : 我要让你去恨某些人，因为我想打动你。做法之一，就是让你重新审视那些立场并不那么坚定的角色。

lines.en: : {b}Question 5: Because Prisoner was such a big event in the game, did you spend extra time on it to get it exactly how you wanted?{/b}
lines.zh: : {b}问题五：《囚徒》在游戏里分量这么重，你有没有在它上面多花时间，好把它做成你想要的样子？{/b}

lines.en: : Prisoner was, if I’m remembering correctly, the longest event in the game for a long time. Which meant it took the longest to get exactly how I wanted it to be.
lines.zh: : 如果我没记错的话，《囚徒》在很长一段时间里是游戏里最长的事件。也就是说，为了把它调成我想要的样子，花的时间也最长。

lines.en: : I’m pretty sure I spent an entire day on this event alone, but I {i}needed{/i} it to be perfect since it was the first big “earth shattering” interpersonal moment in the game, save maybe This Town Has Two Halves.
lines.zh: : 我几乎能确定，光这一个事件我就花了一整天。但我{i}必须{/i}让它完美，因为除了《这座小镇有两半》之外，它是游戏里第一个「天崩地裂」式的人际关系时刻。

lines.en: : {b}Question 6: How much thought/dread do you put into it each time you add another flag you’re going to have to account for the rest of the game?{/b}
lines.zh: : {b}问题六：每加一个后面整部游戏都得记着的 flag，你会花多少心力，又会有多少「又要来了」的恐惧？{/b}

lines.en: : There’s a good amount of thought that goes into this and, while it would be cool to say that it doesn’t matter to me so long as it’s right for the story, that’s not exactly true.
lines.zh: : 这确实要花不少心思。虽然说「只要对故事合适我就无所谓」听起来很酷，但我并不真的那么想。

lines.en: : There are plenty of times where I’ve decided against incorporating flags that send the game down multiple, deviating paths- but this was one of the times I believed it was both worth it and {i}possible.{/i}
lines.zh: : 有很多次我决定不加入那些会让游戏分出多条岔路的 flag——但这一次，我认为它既值得、也{i}做得到{/i}。

lines.en: : I love working by myself, but an important part of that is understanding exactly how much I can handle.
lines.zh: : 我喜欢一个人干活，但其中很重要的一点是：要清楚自己到底扛得住多少。

lines.en: : With that in mind, I never really {i}dread{/i} it as I’m always excited to see where both directions of the story go afterward.
lines.zh: : 抱着这个想法，我其实从不{i}害怕{/i}——因为我总是很兴奋地想看故事两条路各自会走向哪里。

lines.en: : {b}Final Question:{/b}
lines.zh: : {b}最后一个问题：{/b}

lines.en: : {b}Seeing how this was the first example of a character extremely sexually assaulting another, were you worried at all by how that would be received by the community?{/b}
lines.zh: : {b}考虑到这是游戏里第一次出现一个角色对另一个角色实施严重性侵，你一点都不担心玩家会怎么接受吗？{/b}

lines.en: : At first, I think I probably was.
lines.zh: : 一开始，我想大概是担心的。

lines.en: : As a creator, I’ve always loved pushing boundaries and telling stories about things many others don’t feel comfortable with. And the use of visuals is able to elevate that in an amazing and haunting way.
lines.zh: : 作为一个创作者，我一直喜欢越界，喜欢讲那些很多人觉得不舒服的故事。而画面的运用能把这一点提升到一种惊人且挥之不去的程度。

lines.en: : But when your livelihood depends entirely on {i}one{/i} thing that you are creating, you can’t help but worry about things like this.
lines.zh: : 但当你的生计完全押在{i}一个{/i}你正在做的东西上时，你没法不为这种事担心。

lines.en: : I had {i}just{/i} gone full time on Lessons in Love for the release of this event. And if people did not receive it well and pulled support, I would have had to go back to my old job.
lines.zh: : 为了发布这个事件，我{i}刚刚{/i}转成全职做《Lessons in Love》。如果大家接受不了、撤了支持，我就得回去干老本行。

lines.en: : But at the end of the day, people both trusted and admired my vision for this game. They understood the story I was telling and, today, I no longer have fears like that.
lines.zh: : 但说到底，人们信任我、也欣赏我对这游戏的方向。他们看懂了我在讲的故事，所以今天我已经没有那种恐惧了。

lines.en: : And there is not {i}anything{/i} I am afraid of incorporating so long as it helps me get my point across or make you feel something.
lines.zh: : 只要能帮我把想说的说清楚、能让你感受到什么，就没有{i}任何{/i}东西是我不敢写进去的。

lines.en: scene black
Thank you again for taking the time out of your day to read the scene commentary for Ayane Amamiya’s event, “Prisoner.”
lines.zh: 再次感谢你抽出时间读 Ayane Amamiya 事件《囚徒》的场景解说。

lines.en: It is the first time I’ve ever done something like this, so I do hope it was enjoyable as I would like to include more things like this in future care packages.
lines.zh: 这是我第一次做这样的事，所以希望你觉得有意思——因为我想在之后的内容包里多放些类似的东西。

lines.en: But for now, please go back to enjoying Lessons in Love while {i}I{/i} go back to creating it.
lines.zh: 但现在，请你继续享受《Lessons in Love》，而{i}我{/i}回去继续做它。

lines.en: Selebus, signing off.
lines.zh: Selebus，下线。
